title: Fix issues #573 and #574 — braceless if siblings and else-if chains do not add nesting

intentCoverage.report:
Intent Coverage report (verbatim):

**Verdict: Caught.** The existing tests catch a regression where `else if` piles up twice. I removed the scratch worktree and confirmed it is gone.

**What was checked**
- Story: `.planning/seeds/SEED-061-fix-issues-573-574-nesting-depth.md#fix-issues-573-574-nesting-depth`, revision 09e9704c77e8aabc697e4eb680d7d24704e08b52.
- Promise: NS (-Ens) counts an `else if` chain as one structure (#574), and a structure really nested inside an else-if branch still counts.
- Scratch: a detached worktree of 09e9704c at `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/a2827921/tmp/ic-061`, clean before the probe. I did not touch the execution checkout.
- Before the fault: `nix develop -c python -m pytest -q test/testNestedStructures.py test/testJavaScriptNestedStructures.py` gave 27 passed.

**Fault** (your suggestion; it holds against this revision): in `_after_else` in `lizard_ext/lizardns.py`, I added `else: self.pile_up_within_block()` for the `if` token. That makes `else if` pile up twice again, once there and once in `_in_structure_head`. I left fixtures and assertions unchanged.

**Run with the fault:** 4 failed, 23 passed. These assertions caught it:
- `test/testNestedStructures.py::TestCppNestedStructures::test_else_if`: `assertEqual(1, result[0].max_nested_structures)`
- `test/testNestedStructures.py::TestCppNestedStructures::test_else_if_chain_with_blocks`: `assertEqual(1, result[0].max_nested_structures)`
- `test/testNestedStructures.py::TestCppNestedStructures::test_structure_nested_in_else_if_branch`: `assertEqual(2, result[0].max_nested_structures)`
- `test/testJavaScriptNestedStructures.py::TestJavaScriptNestedStructures::test_else_if_chain_is_one_structure`: an `assertEqual` on NS

**Independent check of the wrong behaviour:** a scratch script ran `FileAnalyzer` with the lizardns extension on the C++ chain `if(a){} else if(b){} else if(c){} else {}`. It reported NS = 3 with the fault and 1 after restoring, so the chain really stopped counting as one structure. This result covers only the double-pile fault. I did not run the other fault you suggested (swallowing the `if` without piling).

**Restore and cleanup**
- `git checkout -- lizard_ext/lizardns.py`, then `git status --short` was empty.
- The script gave 1 again, and the same test command gave 27 passed.
- I removed the worktree with `git worktree remove --force`; `--force` was needed because of the untracked nix `.venv`. `git worktree list` no longer shows it, the directory is gone, and the temporary script is deleted.

**Next proof action:** none for this promise and fault. No planned repair matched, and the probe leads to no new repair decision.

**Costs**
- **Test runtime (measured, pytest wall time, excluding nix startup):** 1.63 s before the fault, 0.58 s with it, 0.63 s after restoring.
- **Human effort:** unavailable; no human took part in this run.
- **Agent effort:** unavailable; I have no supported way to measure it. The run took 4 tool calls before the report.
- **Invocation-to-report elapsed (measured):** 201,780 ms (epoch ms 1794917086539 to 1794917288319).

Wrap-up disposition: 09e9704c77e8aabc697e4eb680d7d24704e08b52, Caught, no follow-up.
